stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Meera is at floor 1.
2. Aarav is exactly 3 positions above Ravi.
3. Uma is exactly 2 positions above Kavya.
4. In the stated ordering, Uma comes before Bharat, and Bharat comes before Jai.
stimuli.solution: floor 1: Meera; floor 2: Kavya; floor 3: Ravi; floor 4: Uma; floor 5: Bharat; floor 6: Aarav; floor 7: Jai

stimuli.title: Seven people have interviews in seven consecutive months from January to July, one per month.

stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).

stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:

stimuli.solution: honest=li, window=fa, thunder=ka, temple=te, summer=no, paper=sa

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain X < V > W ≤ U < T, decide which conclusions follow. I: W ≤ U. II: W < T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Q > P < W < X ≤ Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: P ≤ W. II: Q < X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain X < S < V ≤ P < U, decide which conclusions follow. I: V > U. II: X ≤ V.

questions.stem: Statements: All sailors are readers. No readers are painters. Conclusions: I. No sailors are painters. II. Some sailors are painters. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: A is contained in B, while B and C are disjoint.

questions.stem: Statements: Some coders are workers. No workers are readers. Conclusions: I. Some coders are not readers. II. All coders are readers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The A∩B members cannot be C.

questions.stem: Statements: Some artists are runners. Some runners are teachers. Conclusions: I. Some artists are teachers. II. Some runners are artists. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The two Some overlaps need not coincide; Some A are B converts to Some B are A.

questions.stem: Statements: All poets are dancers. Some workers are poets. Conclusions: I. Some workers are dancers. II. Some dancers are workers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No farmers are sailors. All coders are sailors. Some coders are sailors. Conclusions: I. No farmers are coders. II. Some coders are not farmers. Which conclusion follows?

questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 95 km north, then 76 km east, then 19 km south and finally 19 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net north = 76 km and east = 57 km. Distance = √(76²+57²) = 95 km.

questions.stem: Kiran moves 19 km north, 114 km east, 57 km south and 19 km west. In which direction is Kiran from the start?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 171 km north, 76 km east, 95 km south and 19 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?
questions.explanation: Total path length = 171+76+95+19=361 km (not displacement).
